name_ar: طابق شكل التعليمة مع نوع الفشل واختبر الصياغة باختبارات دقيقة
name_en: Match the instruction form to the failure, then micro-test the wording
what: قبل كتابة أي قاعدة في مهارة أو برومبت، صنّف الفشل الملاحظ واختر الشكل المناسب له (منع، وصفة، خانة إلزامية، شرط)، ثم اختبر الصياغة مقابل نسخة بلا توجيه. — Classify the observed failure, pick the instruction form that fixes that failure type, and micro-test the wording against a no-guidance control before shipping it.
when: كتابة قاعدة في مهارة، البرومبت يتجاهل تعليمة، المخرج شكله غلط / writing a rule into a skill or prompt, a rule keeps being ignored, output has the wrong shape
how: 1) Run the task without the new guidance first; if the failure does not appear, write nothing. 2) Classify the failure: skips a known rule under pressure → short prohibition plus a table of the excuses seen and a red-flags list; right behaviour but wrong output shape → a positive recipe that states the parts of the output in order (prohibitions here make it worse); a required element is missing → a required slot in the template being filled; behaviour should depend on a condition → a conditional keyed to an observable fact ('if the brief exists, cite it'). 3) No nuance clauses ('don't X unless it matters') and no exemption clauses ('this limit doesn't apply to code'): they reopen negotiation or leak; restructure so the rule cannot reach the exempt part. 4) Give every rule its reason in one clause; reasons transfer to unseen cases where bare rules do not. 5) End a reference list with a non-exhaustive licence ('covers common cases; reason from the whys'), and mark any enumerated read-list as a floor, otherwise the list becomes the model's blind spot. 6) Prefer a strong pretrained word ('tight', 'red', 'relentless') over a restated triad; say the target behaviour positively and keep negatives only as hard guardrails. 7) Micro-test: one fresh context per sample, the real surrounding skill as context, a task that tempts the failure, 5+ samples per variant plus the no-guidance control; read every flagged hit by hand. 8) Variance is a metric: if 5 samples give 5 interpretations, tighten the form before adding words. 9) Calm craft register: threat/urgency language and ALL-CAPS drive corner-cutting. Failure modes go in the skill only after they really happened. name_ar: صمّم شكل المهارة: نمط الاستدعاء وتصنيف الخطوات ومعيار الإنجاز وقسم المطبّات
name_en: Design a skill's shape: invocation mode, step typing, completion criteria, growing gotchas
what: قرارات بنية المهارة قبل كتابة نصها: من يستدعيها، أي خطوة كود وأيها استدلال وأيها قرار بشري، ومتى تُعتبر كل خطوة منتهية. — Structural decisions for a skill before writing prose: who invokes it, which steps are code vs model reasoning vs human decision, and a checkable done-condition per step.
when: إنشاء مهارة جديدة أو تقسيم مهارة كبيرة / creating a new skill, splitting a big skill, a skill whose steps get rushed
how: 1) Pick one category per skill (reference, verification, data/analysis, automation, scaffolding, review, deploy, runbook, ops); a skill straddling several is confused. 2) Invocation: model-invoked only if the agent or another skill must reach it alone (its description is paid every turn); otherwise user-invoked with a one-line human description, and when manual skills multiply add one router skill. 3) Description = trigger condition with one phrase per distinct branch, the neighbour skill named in a NOT-for clause; never a workflow summary. 4) Type each step code / inference / hybrid / human; any output that must be byte-identical on rerun (tables, sorting, templates) goes to a script; every inference step states input, output and why code can't do it. 5) Who-does-what table plus explicit human confirmation points; never proceed on silence; missing values stay null, unreadable inputs go to a separate list. 6) Each step ends with a checkable, exhaustive completion criterion ('every modified file accounted for'); if the agent still rushes, split the later steps out so they are not in view. 7) Hub SKILL.md short; spokes one level deep, each link saying when to read it; inline what every branch needs, push behind pointers what only some branches use. 8) Start a Gotchas section and add one line every time Claude trips; it becomes the highest-signal part. 9) First-run setup in a config file (ask if missing); persistent state outside the skill folder; optional session-scoped hooks for guardrails. 10) Status labels honestly: needs-verification until behaviour was tested. name_en: Skillify a finished session into a reusable workflow skill
what: بعد إنجاز عمل متكرر (مونتاج ريل، حزمة برومبتات)، استخرج خطواته ومدخلاته ومعايير نجاح كل خطوة وتصحيحات المستخدم إلى مهارة، أو إلى ذاكرة إن كان مجرد معلومة. — After a repeated job is done, capture its steps, inputs, per-step success criteria and the user's corrections as a skill — or as a memory note if it is only a fact.
when: 'احفظ ده كمهارة'، 'إيه اللي اتعلمناه'، نفس الشغل اتكرر في أكثر من جلسة / 'save this as a skill', 'what did we learn', same workflow repeated across sessions

name_ar: ملف صوت المالك: قابل للقياس ومدعوم باقتباسات وينمو من تعديلاته
name_en: Owner voice file: measurable, quote-backed, grows from edits
what: ملف صوت قصير يصف كيف يكتب/يتكلم المالك بأرقام واقتباسات لا بصفات — Build a ≤150-line voice file from 3–5 of the owner's own pieces that every writing skill loads.
when: اكتب بصوتي، الريل لازم يبقى بطريقتي، out/voice.md / write like me, my voice, voice profile, before any reel script
how: 1) Collect 3–5 of the owner's own pieces in the SAME genre but DIFFERENT topics (same-topic samples narrow the range and hurt); <3 → mark confidence: low; 0 → refuse. 2) Measure, don't describe: median sentence length and spread, shortest sentence, paragraph length, connector rate, concrete-anchor density, dialect markers (مش/هـ/اللي), digit system, dash/emoji rate. 3) Habits section: how he opens, gives examples, signals doubt, closes — each habit must quote one real line; no quote → drop the habit. 4) Never-say list: words/structures that appear 0 times in his samples but are common model defaults, each with his replacement (not just a ban). 5) 3–5 positive excerpts + 1 negative: the model's own default draft on the same topic with a line on what differs (contrastive example). 6) No personality adjectives (دافئ/حاد) — they are not checkable. 7) Use it as completion: continue his text rather than 'imitate his style'. 8) Update loop: after each session diff his edits against the draft; corrections that repeat become new never-say/habit lines with a dated log entry; do not rewrite the whole file. 9) If samples disagree strongly (e.g. caption vs voiceover), keep two profiles instead of averaging. 10) Only the owner's own voice (or a team he represents) — never a named third party. name_ar: إعادة كتابة على مستوى الخطاب مع قارئ بارد معزول
name_en: Discourse-level rewrite with an isolated cold reader
what: إصلاح ما يجعل القارئ يفقد الخيط رغم فهمه كل كلمة — Fix the thread, not the vocabulary: old→new flow, topic chain, emphasis position, lists that replace argument; judged by a fresh-context reader.
when: النص مفهوم كلمة كلمة بس مش ماشي، القارئ بيتوه / reader loses the thread, reads like AI after word-level cleanup
how: 1) Three layers: words (WRITE-02/03 scans), syntax (nominalised shells like تم القيام بـ, participle tails, uniform length), discourse (this card). 2) Paragraph checks: first sentence = the paragraph's claim (reading first sentences alone must carry the piece); each sentence starts with something already known and puts the new item at the end; one key term reused, never rotated. 3) Document checks: the trigger/problem with a date or number opens, the decision appears within 3 paragraphs, no closing summary paragraph, delete-test (a paragraph whose removal loses nothing is a repeat), headings as claims not category names. 4) A list whose items depend on each other (premise, cause, trade-off) becomes prose with the relation words; scan-read genres (reports, README, reference) keep their skeleton — edit sentences only and diff heading levels, list item counts and table shapes before/after. 5) The only allowed information gain is digging out specifics already in the source; missing ones become [يحتاج تحقق: …]. 6) Certainty check: count hedges/commitments before and after; 'سوف' must not become 'قد' or vice versa. 7) Review in a separate agent that gets only the rewrite, the reader and the genre (never the source or the brief); it reports per paragraph: expected / got / where lost. 8) Max 2 rounds; still failing → deliver with the list of paragraphs that need the author to add content, not more polishing. 9) For key openings: draft 5 candidates, drop the most predictable one first (typicality bias), then choose. name_ar: إصلاح الترجمة الحرفية في العربية بعد الترجمة أو التعريب
name_en: Arabic translationese repair after translation or localization
what: تنعيم نص عربي مترجم دون تغيير معناه أو سجله — Post-edit translated Arabic (scripts, subtitles, UI strings) to remove calques while locking facts, modality and register.
when: النص مترجم وباين، ترجمة حرفية، تعريب واجهة، ترجمة سكريبت أو ترجمة / translationese, calques, localize UI, translated subtitles
how: 1) Translate first, naturalize second; never do both in one pass. For long sources: pin a glossary (key terms, chapter/section titles, names) before translating, translate per section, sanity-check length ratio per section, and read one finished section against the source before running the rest. 2) Mask protected spans byte-for-byte: numbers, dates, URLs, code, names, placeholders like {count}, quotes. 3) Calque families to fix: يلعب دورًا/يعتبر بمثابة → plain verb; من خلال/عن طريق chains; تمّ + مصدر → named actor; بالإضافة إلى ذلك/علاوة على ذلك at every paragraph; human adverbs on programs (بصمت، بشفافية، بأناقة) → say what actually happens; English word order (adjective chains, sentence-final 'حيث'); English punctuation (, ? ; and em dashes). 4) Lock modality: must stays يجب, may stays قد; conditions, negations, order unchanged. 5) Keep register (MSA vs Egyptian) and one spelling/digit convention; do not convert. 6) Edit budget: character change ≲30% normal, 30–50% re-verify every claim, >50% stop — you are rewriting, not naturalizing. 7) UI-string mode suspends the budget: labels become noun phrases, short and uniform within one screen; but never add a behavior or warning the source did not state; unknown term → flag, leave as is. 8) Arabic plural/gender: ICU needs zero/one/two/few/many/other; check every category reads naturally. 9) Optional: keep a per-owner rules file (signal, exception, rewrite) that grows from his corrections; apply only when context matches. 10) Report: final text, then only 'needs check' items. name_ar: بنك القصص: مقابلة تحفظ الأرقام ونقاط التحول والمواقف
name_en: Story bank interview: numbers, turning points, positions
what: مقابلة مرة واحدة تملأ ملفًا دائمًا بالمادة الحقيقية للمحتوى — One structured interview fills a persistent story bank so hooks never need invented facts.
when: مش لاقي أقول إيه، اعملي مقابلة، الفكرة رفيعة / interview me, I have nothing to post, thin idea, the one true thing
how: 1) Read the bank first; ask only thin sections — never re-ask. 2) Open wide with one question and follow what he gets animated about; one question at a time. 3) Press every soft answer exactly once: 'improved' → by how much, over what period; 'a while ago' → which month; 'a big client' → can it be named. 4) Chase the reversal: what he believed a year ago and no longer does, and what it cost. 5) Find the position: what he thinks is true that peers dispute, and the cost of holding it. 6) Collect the 3 stories he already tells in person (pre-tested). 7) Settle naming limits explicitly; 'rather not say' is recorded as off-limits forever. 8) Write verbatim phrasing where vivid, date the file, list thin sections; leave unknown numbers empty, never inferred. 9) Mining a single story: return 3–5 genuinely distinct angles (lesson, contrarian, method, proof, relatable moment) plus 'not worth angling' (e.g. no proof angle until numbers are final); anonymize clients by default; openings start at the surprise/number, never chronology. 10) Post mode: moment not theme → number and date → what he got wrong → who disagrees → what viewer should do; read back a 5-line spine. name_ar: من شرارة إلى فكرة قابلة للتصوير: احتمالات، لوجلاين، رهانات
name_en: From spark to filmable premise: what-ifs, logline tests, stakes
what: تحويل صورة أو إحساس إلى فرضية فيلم/ريل تحمل صراعًا — Turn a spark into a premise that can carry a short film or series before any boards.
when: عندي فكرة فيلم، لو حصل كذا، هل الفكرة قوية / film idea, what if, is this premise strong, logline
how: 1) Record the spark in his words and classify it: image, what-if, character, setting, feeling; ask what drew him — that answer must survive later changes. 2) Generate 8–12 what-ifs by angle: invert it, raise the cost, move it in time or place, give it to the wrong person; flag which already imply conflict; he picks 1–3. 3) Logline = protagonist + want + obstacle + stakes. 4) Stress tests, each pass/weak/fail with one reason and one fix: active protagonist, opposition that can win, a choice at the end, personal stakes, situation that sustains the target length (5 s, 30 s, 3 min, series). 5) Stakes on three levels: external, relational, internal; at least two concrete. 6) Controlling idea + its counter-argument as working hypotheses. 7) For a contrarian angle: decompose into falsifiable claims, attack each; if objections reduce it to a tautology it is not an insight; refine to more precise wording, never retreat to weaker. 8) Hand a one-screen brief (title, logline, stakes, form, language/dialect) to STORY-01 intake. name_ar: حرفة مشهد الحوار: نص فرعي، ادخل متأخرًا، فعل مرئي فقط
name_en: Dialogue scene craft: subtext, late entry, visible-only action
what: قواعد كتابة مشاهد وحوار لفيلم قصير أو إعلان تمثيلي — Rules and model tells for scripted scenes with characters.
when: سكريبت فيه حوار، مشهد بين شخصيتين، فيلم قصير، إعلان تمثيلي / dialogue scene, short film script, screenplay
how: 1) Every scene: someone wants something, something blocks it, the situation ends changed; outcomes yes-but / no-and / no-but; a clean yes kills tension. 2) Enter late, leave early: cut arrivals, greetings, goodbyes, and the summarizing last line. 3) Action lines in present tense, only what can be seen or heard, ≤3–4 lines; never 'she feels devastated'. 4) Subtext: characters talk around the thing; nobody answers the question directly; nobody explains what both know ('as you know…'). 5) Each character has a verbal signature (rhythm, words, what they never say, register/dialect fixed per pair — a shift is a story event); cover names and you should still know who speaks. 6) Monologues ≤5 lines; one physical reaction at most; withhold one thing per scene. 7) Model tells to scan: characters stating motive or theme, convenient coincidences, emotion on schedule, uniform scene length, final scene mirroring the first with one word changed, metaphors that explain themselves. 8) Timing: ~1 page ≈ 1 minute; for shorts one turn, no subplot. 9) Voiceover/audiobook version: add a pronunciation respelling list for names, and re-read for what fails aloud (visual-only jokes, tables, long untagged dialogue). what: جمع شذرات بلا ترتيب ثم بناء النص فقرة فقرة على مفاهيم مؤسسة — Separate idea-mining from shaping; build explainer scripts block by block on grounded concepts.

what: مراجعة نص تسويقي/كابشن بتمريرات منفصلة لكل بُعد — Review existing copy one dimension per pass, re-checking earlier passes after each fix.
when: راجع الكابشن، حسن النص الإعلاني، الكوبي ضعيف / review my caption, improve ad copy
how: 0) Mechanical pass first: throat-clearing openers (في عالم اليوم، لا يخفى على أحد), binary contrast (مش بس… ده), dramatic fragments (وبس. كده.), empty jargon, stacked triads; report density per 100 words (<0.5 ok, 0.5–1.5 revise, >1.5 rewrite the passage). 1) Clarity: mark what doesn't land on first read before proposing. 2) Voice: audit against the voice file; compare start vs end for tone drift. 3) So-what: every claim answers why the viewer should care. 4) Prove: superlatives need a source; no proof → soften the claim, never invent it. 5) Specificity: vague → numbers/timeframes from the source; can't be specific → cut. 6) Emotion: concrete before-state, no fake urgency. 7) Zero risk near the CTA: unanswered objection, unclear next step. After each sweep re-run the earlier ones. Output: per-line current/proposed/reason, a 'kept on purpose' list, then the full revised text. Severity: high = meaning/legal/hidden action, medium = comprehension/trust, low = polish.
